articles.body: Here's a made-up shift at a plant that inspects welded frames (every name, time and setting in this post is illustrative). An inspector starts an inspection on frame A118 at 11:20 with a handheld camera. The vision model flags a weld gap, the inspector confirms it, and because the org's rules don't ask for a close-up photo yet, they log the finding and move on to the next section. At 11:40 the quality lead changes an org setting: from now on every finding needs a close-up photo. Reasonable change. They made it for the next batch. At 11:55 the inspector taps Complete on A118 : 11:55:02 POST /inspections/insp-7/complete 11:55:02 422 {"error": "close-up photo required for: weld_gap"} The weld gap was logged 35 minutes earlier under rules that didn't ask for a photo.

articles.title: Goldcrest: Conversational State to Monte Carlo Parameters
articles.excerpt: Goldcrest is a household financial planning tool that replaces spreadsheet forms with a conversational interface. You answer short questions in a chat. The agent extracts income, expenses, asset value…
articles.body: Goldcrest is a household financial planning tool that replaces spreadsheet forms with a conversational interface. You answer short questions in a chat. The agent extracts income, expenses, asset values, and timeline assumptions, then feeds them into a Monte Carlo simulation that projects your financial trajectory across thousands of market paths. The interesting plumbing is the boundary between the LLM-driven conversation layer and the deterministic financial engine. The agent must maintain dialogue state across multiple turns, validate inputs, resolve ambiguity, and serialize a complete parameter set without letting the LLM touch arithmetic or generate advice.

articles.title: When Your Agent Leaves the Process: What Strands A2A Reveals About Cross-Process Token Accounting and Failure Reporting
articles.excerpt: When you move an agent from a local function call to a remote HTTP endpoint, you lose three things: shared memory, a unified token ledger, and a single failure surface. Strands A2A, an open protocol f…
articles.body: When you move an agent from a local function call to a remote HTTP endpoint, you lose three things: shared memory, a unified token ledger, and a single failure surface. Strands A2A, an open protocol for agent-to-agent communication, exposes these gaps with production telemetry from nine real runs. The evidence is specific. A caller reports zero tokens for a run that consumed 2369 on the remote side. A remote tool raises an exception, yet the orchestrator marks the task completed. A reply times out, but the receipt already exists on disk. These are not edge cases. They are the default behavior when orchestration crosses process boundaries without new accounting primitives. The Setup: Two Processes, One Port, No Shared Ledger The test task is minimal.

articles.title: How to Verify Customer Domain Records in Go — 3 Onboarding Gates
articles.excerpt: Zone access is the constraint that changes custom domain onboarding UX. Short answer: write DNS records only where you control the zone; otherwise show the exact records to copy and a verification act…
articles.body: Zone access is the constraint that changes custom domain onboarding UX. Short answer: write DNS records only where you control the zone; otherwise show the exact records to copy and a verification action. For healthtech mail, keep SPF, DKIM, and DMARC publication evidence separate from evidence that messages are actually delivered. Consider a bounded design exercise, not a reported incident: a healthtech platform is onboarding 30 clinic domains, 10 in zones it manages and 20 held by clinic administrators. In reviewing that rollout, I would stop the activation decision at three checks: authority to change DNS, observed configuration, and delivery evidence. Those counts are planning inputs, not customer results.

articles.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
articles.excerpt: The answer to one of Earth's greatest geological mysteries may lie deep beneath our feet.
articles.body: More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged.

articles.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
articles.excerpt: United Launch Alliance has traced the Nov. 15 failure of its Vulcan Centaur rocket to an inadequate supply of propellant to the vehicle's first-stage engines.
articles.body: United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4.
